How I work

I work across the parts that usually get split between teams.

I design the platform and I help build it. That usually means setting up the foundation, moving workloads onto it, keeping costs in check, and making sure it stays healthy after launch.

[01]

Cloud foundations
& DevOps

Turning scattered AWS accounts into one well-run platform, with Terraform, CI/CD, a clear account structure, networking, and guardrails that make the safe option the easy one.

In practice Standardize the cloud Build the delivery engine

[02]

Migration &
modernization

Moving old databases and monolithic apps in careful stages, so the business keeps running while the new setup gains better recovery options and gets easier to operate.

In practice Database migration and connection pooling Cut database read load

[03]

Security, identity

Setting clear authentication and authorization boundaries, automating releases, and layering controls so security doesn't hinge on one app or on someone remembering a manual step.

Tying cost back to design decisions: right-sizing, caching, monitoring, and automatic recovery, so systems stay up and people spend less time fighting fires.

In practice Mail disaster recovery Trace an EKS ingress incident

WBS · ITIL change control

How a change reaches production

Every change leaves a record of what changed, who approved it, and how to undo it.

  1. 01

    Scope it

    A work breakdown structure: work packages, owners, dependencies, and the order they land in.

    Sequenced wave roadmap
  2. 02

    Raise the change

    A change request with the risk, the rollback plan, and CAB approval before anything is scheduled.

    Regulated CI/CD delivery
  3. 03

    Prove it

    Review the plan output and rehearse outside production, so the real run holds no surprises.

    Keep Aurora DR in parity
  4. 04

    Ship it

    Roll out in stages inside the agreed window, with the rollback ready rather than improvised.

    Rolling patches on Oracle RAC
  5. 05

    Verify and review

    Check the outcome, not just that the deploy finished, then close it with a post-implementation review.

    Silent CDR ingestion failure
